identity.name: Acetic acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
synonyms: Acetic and fatty acid esters of glycerol
identity.chemical_class: Mixture of acetylated mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids (glycerol esters)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic glyceride esters lower oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize dispersed fat-water systems.
common_food_categories: general food uses under good manufacturing practice / technical-effect levels
food-processing, food-packing, and food-storage equipment uses permitted by regulation

adi.basis: EFSA (2020) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI for E472a,b,c; 2025 follow-up focused on specification updates.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation found no adverse effects relevant for humans and no need for a numerical ADI for E472a; the 2025 specifications opinion did not identify a safety concern under proposed impurity limits.

fda.notes: Listed as a direct food additive with defined manufacturing/specification/use conditions; not GRAS-affirmed under Part 184 by this specific name in the accessed Title 21 text.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI: NOT LIMITED (group context with total tartaric acid intake caveat).

concerns.summary: Recent mouse work on common emulsifiers reported dysbiosis/metabolic effects, including for mono- and diglycerides; evidence is indirect for E472a specifically.
A large prospective cohort linked higher intake of E471 (mono- and diglycerides) with some cancer outcomes; observational and not specific to E472a.
Modern E472a-specific human safety datasets are limited; current confidence relies mainly on regulatory toxicology and grouped ester evaluations.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA (2020) identified no adverse effects relevant for humans and no need for a numerical ADI for E472a,b,c.
EFSA (2025) follow-up on specifications for E472a,b,d,e,f did not identify safety concern under proposed impurity limits.
JECFA evaluation set ADI to NOT LIMITED for this additive group context.
U.S. regulation allows use under 21 CFR 172.828 with explicit manufacturing/specification conditions and technical-effect limit language.

populations: no E472a-specific numerical ADI population exceedance identified
children and infants were considered in EFSA exposure/specification contexts
adi_exceedance.notes: ADI exceedance cannot be computed numerically for E472a because EFSA did not set a numerical ADI for E472a and JECFA uses NOT LIMITED.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations (EFSA/JECFA/FDA) remain broadly reassuring at permitted uses, but limited contemporary E472a-specific human evidence and indirect emulsifier-class concerns argue against classifying as risk_free.
key_factors: EFSA no numerical ADI needed for E472a in 2020 re-evaluation
EFSA 2025 specification follow-up found no new safety concern under proposed limits
FDA/eCFR authorizes use under 21 CFR 172.828 with conditions
No IARC classification entry found for E472a or key synonyms
Recent concern signals are mostly indirect (broader emulsifier class, not E472a-specific)
